newsitem.title: JAPAN: FORECAST - Japan April M2+CDs growth seen 2.5%-2.8%.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Japan April M2+CDs growth seen 2.5%-2.8%.

text.p: Japan's money supply growth is likely to have remained sluggish at between 2.5 percent and 2.8 percent in April, reflecting the negative impact on the economy of the rise in the sales tax, economists polled by Reuters said on Tuesday.

Jeffrey Young, an economist specialising in economic and market analysis at Salomon Brothers Asia Ltd, said that Japan's broadly defined money supply average of M2 plus certificates of deposit (M2+CDs) was likely to have fallen in April due to a decline in economic activity.
"The economy slowed sharply in April...spending at least did, so it stands to reason that money probably did, too," Young said.
Japan's consumption tax rate was increased to five percent from three percent on April 1.
Another factor preventing M2+CDs from rising further in April was a flow of funds into foreign bonds, said Ryo Sawai, an economist for Yamaichi Research Institute.
"The yen was weak against the dollar in April, and this spurred investment in foreign bonds. Such investment in instruments outside the M2+CDs category prevented its further rise," Sawai said.
Economists' forecasts for year-on-year growth in the M2+CDs money supply average in April ranged from 2.5 percent to 2.8 percent.
Economists said that a lack of significant growth in bank lending was another factor capping rises in M2+CDs.
"There has not been sufficient improvement in bank lending to offset the (negative) factor in April, which is very weak consumer spending," said Young at Salomon Brothers.
Although bank lending seemed to have stopped decelerating, there had only been weak growth, he added.
